top_authentic_signals.name: Thermal Noise & Sensor Consistency
top_authentic_signals.summary: The image shows consistent, subtle grain in nearly all regions (1.0% smooth blocks, variance 6728.5) - the expected fingerprint of a real camera sensor.
top_authentic_signals.what_found: Only 1.0% of pixel blocks are flat - the rest carry a consistent, fine-grained texture at the sub-pixel level. This is the natural noise floor left by photon shot noise and thermal read noise on real camera sensors. The variance of 6728.5 is healthy: present but controlled, suggesting base-ISO capture with standard noise reduction.
top_authentic_signals.why_it_matters: Uniform, subtle grain that's present everywhere but never overwhelming is genuinely difficult for AI to replicate convincingly. This pattern - real grain without being suspiciously chaotic - is one of the stronger authentic fingerprints this test can find.
top_authentic_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, upscaling, or added grain filters can all change the noise profile independently of whether the image was generated or photographed.

top_ai_signals.name: Live Web Fact-Checking (OSINT)
top_ai_signals.summary: The research agent found credible public sources flagging this image or claim as fabricated.
top_ai_signals.what_found: The image depicting Pope Francis in a white puffer coat is an artificial intelligence (AI) generated deepfake, created using the Midjourney program. It first appeared on Reddit's r/midjourney subreddit on March 24, 2023, under titles like "The Pope Drip." Fact-checking organizations such as Snopes, Business Insider, and Forbes quickly debunked the image, confirming it was not a real photograph. The image went viral, fooling many social media users, and Pope Francis himself later referenced being the subject of such AI-generated images, warning about a "crisis of truth." The creator stated it was made for humor.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Named fact-checks and dated public provenance are stronger than a naked model score because they show where the claim came from and whether journalists have already verified or debunked it.
top_ai_signals.caveat: OSINT is strongest for public figures, viral claims, and news events. Generic private images may have no searchable provenance.

top_ai_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_ai_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 94.5% AI and 5.5% authentic, a extremely high-confidence finding toward synthetic generation.
top_ai_signals.what_found: All six spectral lenses, covering visual texture (ConvNeXt), frequency grids (FFT), sensor noise simulation (SRM), color-space fingerprints (YCbCr), spatial reconstruction (SPAI), and robustness testing, collectively scored this image 94.5% AI. A score this strong, the majority of lenses independently flagged patterns like periodic frequency grids and noise distributions inconsistent with any known camera sensor profile.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This model looks for patterns invisible to the human eye, buried in the pixel-level math of the image. A 94.5% score means the statistical fingerprint aligns significantly more with AI generation than camera physics, and these frequency-domain traces are very hard to remove without visibly degrading the image.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.
